chapter: Ellington, Gil Evans and first own groups
title: Sam Woodyard
summary: He explains he already knew Sam Woodyard through Charlie Persip and admired his energy and passion.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Four. And Sam was on the others. Was that the first time you met Sam Woodyard too?
Cause he was a…he used to teach Charlie Persip. And Charlie Persip, we used to hang out a lot together, and he’d always talking about Sam.
What did like particularly about Sam Woodyard’s playing?
Well, his energy. He played with a lot of passion. Duke’s Orchestra could have been twice the size it was and Sam could have overpowered everything there. (Laughs) He was a strong drummer.
He used two bass drums, was that anything you thought about doing?
I have enough trouble with one. (Laughs) One is enough for me. (Laughs)
